claim: Human adult muscle-type acetylcholine receptors are heteropentameric ion channels formed from two α-subunits, and one each of the β-, δ-, and ε-subunits.
source: Human adult muscle-type acetylcholine receptors are heteropentameric ion channels formed from two α-subunits, and one each of the β-, δ-, and ε-subunits.
evidence: This is stated directly in the abstract and is established knowledge about AChR structure.

claim: To form functional channels, the AChR subunits must assemble with one another in a precise stoichiometry and arrangement.
source: To form functional channels, the subunits must assemble with one another in a precise stoichiometry and arrangement.
evidence: This is stated in the abstract and reflects established knowledge about AChR assembly requirements.

claim: The four AChR subunits share a common ancestor that is presumed to have formed homopentamers.
source: Despite being different, the four subunits share a common ancestor that is presumed to have formed homopentamers.
evidence: This is stated in the abstract and represents an evolutionary hypothesis based on phylogenetic analysis.

claim: A reconstructed ancestral muscle-type β-subunit can form homopentameric ion channels.
source: Here, we discover that a reconstructed ancestral muscle-type β-subunit can form homopentameric ion channels.
evidence: This is the primary finding stated in the abstract and supported by experimental data throughout the manuscript.

claim: βAnc homopentamers open spontaneously.
source: These homopentamers open spontaneously and display single-channel hallmarks of muscle-type acetylcholine receptor activity.
evidence: This is stated in the abstract and demonstrated by single-channel recordings in the absence of acetylcholine.

claim: βAnc homopentamers display single-channel hallmarks of muscle-type acetylcholine receptor activity.
source: These homopentamers open spontaneously and display single-channel hallmarks of muscle-type acetylcholine receptor activity.
evidence: This is stated in the abstract and supported by kinetic analysis showing burst behavior and nachschlag shuttings.

claim: Signature features of AChR function are independent of agonist.
source: Our findings attest to the homopentameric origin of the muscle-type acetylcholine receptor, and demonstrate that signature features of its function are both independent of agonist and do not necessitate the complex heteropentameric architecture of the modern-day protein.
evidence: This conclusion is stated in the abstract and supported by the observation of AChR-like activity in the absence of acetylcholine.

claim: Signature features of AChR function do not necessitate the complex heteropentameric architecture of the modern-day protein.
source: Our findings attest to the homopentameric origin of the muscle-type acetylcholine receptor, and demonstrate that signature features of its function are both independent of agonist and do not necessitate the complex heteropentameric architecture of the modern-day protein.
evidence: This conclusion is stated in the abstract and supported by the observation that homopentameric βAnc channels exhibit AChR-like properties.

claim: Ligand-gated ion channels convert chemical signals into electrical impulses by coupling the binding of small molecules to the opening of an ion-conducting transmembrane pore.
source: Ligand-gated ion channels convert chemical signals into electrical impulses by coupling the binding of small molecules to the opening of an ion-conducting transmembrane pore (Hille, 2001).
evidence: This is stated in the introduction with a citation to support the established knowledge.

claim: The superfamily of pentameric ligand-gated ion channels (pLGICs) is the largest and most structurally and functionally diverse of ligand-gated channels.
source: Of the many types of ligand-gated channels, the superfamily of pentameric ligand-gated ion channels (pLGICs) is the largest and most structurally and functionally diverse (Jaiteh et al., 2016).
evidence: This is stated in the introduction with a citation to support the claim.

claim: pLGICs are formed from five identical or homologous subunits arranged around a central ion-conducting pore.
source: Formed from five identical or homologous subunits arranged around a central ion-conducting pore, pLGICs are found in almost all forms of life (Corringer et al., 2012).
evidence: This is stated in the introduction with a citation and represents established structural knowledge.

claim: pLGICs are found in almost all forms of life.
source: Formed from five identical or homologous subunits arranged around a central ion-conducting pore, pLGICs are found in almost all forms of life (Corringer et al., 2012).
evidence: This is stated in the introduction with a citation.

claim: In prokaryotes, pLGICs appear to be exclusively homopentameric.
source: In prokaryotes, pLGICs appear to be exclusively homopentameric, while in eukaryotes both homo- and heteropentameric channels are common.
evidence: This is stated in the introduction and represents established knowledge about pLGIC diversity.

claim: In eukaryotes both homo- and heteropentameric pLGIC channels are common.
source: In prokaryotes, pLGICs appear to be exclusively homopentameric, while in eukaryotes both homo- and heteropentameric channels are common.
evidence: This is stated in the introduction and represents established knowledge about pLGIC diversity.

claim: Humans express more than 40 different pLGIC subunits.
source: Humans express more than 40 different pLGIC subunits, which are subdivided based on whether they form cation-selective channels activated by acetylcholine or serotonin (5-hydroxytryptamine [5-HT3]), or anion-selective channels activated by γ-aminobutyric acid or glycine.
evidence: This is stated in the introduction and represents established knowledge about human pLGIC diversity.

claim: Human pLGIC subunits are subdivided based on whether they form cation-selective channels activated by acetylcholine or serotonin, or anion-selective channels activated by γ-aminobutyric acid or glycine.
source: Humans express more than 40 different pLGIC subunits, which are subdivided based on whether they form cation-selective channels activated by acetylcholine or serotonin (5-hydroxytryptamine [5-HT3]), or anion-selective channels activated by γ-aminobutyric acid or glycine.
evidence: This is stated in the introduction and represents established classification of pLGICs.

claim: The repertoire of pLGIC subunits, combined with their ability to form homo- and heteropentamers, leads to a wealth of structural and functional diversity.
source: This repertoire of pLGIC subunits, combined with their ability to form homo- and heteropentamers, leads to a wealth of structural and functional diversity, presumably to meet a variety of synaptic needs (Sine and Engel, 2006).
evidence: This is stated in the introduction with a citation and represents an inference about the functional significance of pLGIC diversity.

claim: The human adult muscle-type AChR is composed of two α-subunits, and one each of the β-, δ-, and ε-subunits.
source: The archetypal pLGIC is the heteropentameric muscle-type nicotinic acetylcholine receptor (AChR), with the human adult form composed of two α-subunits, and one each of the β-, δ-, and ε-subunits (Figure 1; Changeux, 2020a; Changeux, 2020b).
evidence: This is stated in the introduction with citations and shown in Figure 1.

claim: βAnc differs from the human β-subunit by 132 amino acids (approximately 30% of the total amino acid sequence).
source: Previously we resurrected a putative ancestral AChR β-subunit. Referred to as 'βAnc', this subunit differed from its human counterpart by 132 amino acids (i.e. approximately 30% of the total amino acid sequence), yet was able to substitute for the human β-subunit, and also supplant the human δ-subunit, forming functional hybrid ancestral/human AChRs (Emlaw et al., 2021).
evidence: This is stated in the introduction with a citation to previous work.

claim: βAnc was able to substitute for the human β-subunit and also supplant the human δ-subunit, forming functional hybrid ancestral/human AChRs.
source: Previously we resurrected a putative ancestral AChR β-subunit. Referred to as 'βAnc', this subunit differed from its human counterpart by 132 amino acids (i.e. approximately 30% of the total amino acid sequence), yet was able to substitute for the human β-subunit, and also supplant the human δ-subunit, forming functional hybrid ancestral/human AChRs (Emlaw et al., 2021).
evidence: This is stated in the introduction with a citation to previous work.

claim: Hybrid βAnc-containing AChRs are ternary mixtures, containing two βAnc subunits, two human α-subunits, and one human ε-subunit.
source: These hybrid AChRs were ternary mixtures, containing two βAnc subunits, two human α-subunits, and one human ε-subunit.
evidence: This is stated in the introduction and was demonstrated in previous work.

claim: A concatameric construct confirmed that the two βAnc subunits resided next to each other, occupying positions in the heteropentameric complex usually reserved for the human β- and δ-subunits.
source: A concatameric construct confirmed that the two βAnc subunits resided next to each other, occupying positions in the heteropentameric complex usually reserved for the human β- and δ-subunits (Figure 1; Emlaw et al., 2021).
evidence: This is stated in the introduction with a citation and shown in Figure 1.

claim: All pLGIC subunits have both principal (+) and complementary (−) subunit interfaces.
source: Regardless of whether they bind agonist or not, all pLGIC subunits have both principal (+) and complementary (−) subunit interfaces.
evidence: This is stated in the introduction and represents established structural knowledge about pLGICs.

claim: For two neighbouring subunits to sit next to each other, the (+) and (−) interfaces must be structurally compatible.
source: To sit next to each other, the (+) and (−) interfaces of any two neighbouring subunits must be structurally compatible.
evidence: This is stated in the introduction and represents a logical inference from structural principles.

claim: For βAnc to replace both the human β- and δ-subunits, the (+) and (−) interfaces of βAnc must be compatible with each other.
source: Thus, for βAnc to replace both the human β- and δ-subunits, the (+) and (−) interfaces of βAnc must be compatible with each other, raising the possibility that multiple βAnc subunits could coassemble to form βAnc homomers (Figure 1).
evidence: This is stated in the introduction as a logical inference from the observation that βAnc can occupy adjacent positions.

claim: The compatibility of βAnc (+) and (−) interfaces raises the possibility that multiple βAnc subunits could coassemble to form βAnc homomers.
source: Thus, for βAnc to replace both the human β- and δ-subunits, the (+) and (−) interfaces of βAnc must be compatible with each other, raising the possibility that multiple βAnc subunits could coassemble to form βAnc homomers (Figure 1).
evidence: This is stated in the introduction as a hypothesis that is tested in the manuscript.

claim: Reducing the total amount of subunit cDNA in transfections (~sixfold) while maintaining the same 2:1:1:1 subunit cDNA ratio lowered overall AChR expression.
source: In an attempt to lower overall AChR expression with the purpose of facilitating single-channel analysis, we reduced the total amount of subunit cDNA in our transfections (~sixfold), while maintaining the same 2:1:1:1 subunit cDNA ratio (by weight; α:βAnc:δ:ε). Reducing the amount of cDNA lowered overall AChR expression as expected, but also led to heterogeneity in our patches (Figure 2A), which was not present in original single-channel recordings of βAnc-containing AChRs (Prinston et al., 2017).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and shown in Figure 2A.

claim: Reducing the amount of cDNA led to heterogeneity in single-channel patches that was not present in original single-channel recordings of βAnc-containing AChRs.
source: In an attempt to lower overall AChR expression with the purpose of facilitating single-channel analysis, we reduced the total amount of subunit cDNA in our transfections (~sixfold), while maintaining the same 2:1:1:1 subunit cDNA ratio (by weight; α:βAnc:δ:ε). Reducing the amount of cDNA lowered overall AChR expression as expected, but also led to heterogeneity in our patches (Figure 2A), which was not present in original single-channel recordings of βAnc-containing AChRs (Prinston et al., 2017).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section with a citation and shown in Figure 2A.

claim: A second class of channels with a different kinetic signature and increased amplitude was observed when cDNA amount was reduced.
source: Instead of a single population of channels with a uniform amplitude of ~10 pA, and a burst behaviour indicative of βAnc-containing AChRs (Figure 2A; left inset), we also observed a second class of channels with a different kinetic signature, and an increased amplitude (Figure 2A; right inset).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and shown in Figure 2A.

claim: A similar trend was not observed when cDNA encoding the wild-type human β-subunit was cotransfected instead of βAnc.
source: A similar trend was not observed when cDNA encoding the wild-type human β-subunit was cotransfected instead of βAnc (Figure 2—figure supplement 1), indicating that βAnc was the source of the heterogeneity.
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and shown in Figure 2—figure supplement 1.

claim: βAnc was the source of the heterogeneity in single-channel recordings.
source: A similar trend was not observed when cDNA encoding the wild-type human β-subunit was cotransfected instead of βAnc (Figure 2—figure supplement 1), indicating that βAnc was the source of the heterogeneity.
evidence: This is stated in the Results section as an inference from the control experiment.

claim: Lowering the proportion of βAnc cDNA in the transfection mixture reduced the fraction of high amplitude channels.
source: Consistent with this, lowering the proportion of βAnc cDNA in the transfection mixture reduced the fraction of high amplitude channels (Figure 2B and D), while transfecting exclusively with βAnc cDNA resulted in patches where all channel openings had a uniformly high amplitude (Figure 2C and D).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and shown in Figure 2B and D.

claim: Transfecting exclusively with βAnc cDNA resulted in patches where all channel openings had a uniformly high amplitude.
source: Consistent with this, lowering the proportion of βAnc cDNA in the transfection mixture reduced the fraction of high amplitude channels (Figure 2B and D), while transfecting exclusively with βAnc cDNA resulted in patches where all channel openings had a uniformly high amplitude (Figure 2C and D).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and shown in Figure 2C and D.

claim: When transfected alone, βAnc forms functional ion channels.
source: This demonstrated that when transfected alone, βAnc forms functional ion channels.
evidence: This is stated in the Results section as a conclusion from the experimental observations.

claim: In the human adult muscle-type AChR, the agonist-binding sites are located at the α–δ and α–ε interfaces.
source: In the human adult muscle-type AChR, the agonist-binding sites are located at the α–δ and α–ε interfaces, and the β-subunit is the only subunit that does not participate directly in agonist binding (Figure 1; Rahman et al., 2022; Rahman et al., 2020; Zarkadas et al., 2022).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section with citations and shown in Figure 1.

claim: The β-subunit is the only AChR subunit that does not participate directly in agonist binding.
source: In the human adult muscle-type AChR, the agonist-binding sites are located at the α–δ and α–ε interfaces, and the β-subunit is the only subunit that does not participate directly in agonist binding (Figure 1; Rahman et al., 2022; Rahman et al., 2020; Zarkadas et al., 2022).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section with citations.

claim: Channels formed from a muscle-type β-subunit alone would not be expected to have intact agonist-binding sites.
source: We were therefore surprised to see single-channel activity in patches from cells transfected exclusively with βAnc, as channels formed from a muscle-type β-subunit alone would not be expected to have intact agonist-binding sites.
evidence: This is stated in the Results section as an inference from established knowledge about AChR structure.

claim: When no acetylcholine was present, patches from cells transfected exclusively with βAnc cDNA still displayed single-channel activity.
source: When no acetylcholine was present, patches from cells that were transfected exclusively with βAnc cDNA still displayed single-channel activity, indicating that βAnc-alone channels open spontaneously under these conditions (Figure 3A).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and shown in Figure 3A.

claim: βAnc-alone channels open spontaneously in the absence of acetylcholine.
source: When no acetylcholine was present, patches from cells that were transfected exclusively with βAnc cDNA still displayed single-channel activity, indicating that βAnc-alone channels open spontaneously under these conditions (Figure 3A).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section as a conclusion from the observation of activity without agonist.

claim: Spontaneous activity of βAnc-alone channels occurred as bursts of closely spaced openings, separated by brief closings.
source: Furthermore, spontaneous activity occurred as bursts of closely spaced openings, separated by brief closings (Figure 3B; Colquhoun and Hawkes, 1982).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section with a citation and shown in Figure 3B.

claim: The briefest intervening closings in βAnc-alone channels were reminiscent of classic 'nachschlag shuttings' observed in early patch clamp recordings from frog end-plate nicotinic receptors.
source: The briefest of these intervening closings were reminiscent of classic 'nachschlag shuttings' (Figure 3B, 'i' in inset), observed in early patch clamp recordings from frog end-plate nicotinic receptors, and originally thought to relate to agonist efficacy (Colquhoun and Sakmann, 1981).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section with a citation and shown in Figure 3B.

claim: Despite being homomeric and lacking agonist-binding sites, βAnc-alone channels display single-channel hallmarks of the muscle-type AChR.
source: Thus, despite being homomeric and lacking agonist-binding sites, βAnc-alone channels display single-channel hallmarks of the muscle-type AChR.
evidence: This is stated in the Results section as a conclusion from the kinetic observations.

claim: Open duration histograms of βAnc-alone channels were fit well by a single exponential component.
source: Open duration histograms were fit well by a single exponential component, while closed duration histograms required at least two components (Figure 3C).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and shown in Figure 3C.

claim: Closed duration histograms of βAnc-alone channels required at least two exponential components.
source: Open duration histograms were fit well by a single exponential component, while closed duration histograms required at least two components (Figure 3C).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and shown in Figure 3C.

claim: A minimal scheme with a single open state and two closed states is necessary and sufficient to describe the spontaneous activity of βAnc-alone channels.
source: This suggested that a minimal scheme with a single open state and two closed states is necessary and sufficient to describe the spontaneous activity of βAnc-alone channels.
evidence: This is stated in the Results section as an inference from the kinetic analysis.

claim: βAnc-alone channels transition from a closed state, C, to an intermediate closed state, C′, before opening to O′.
source: We settled upon the simple linear scheme, where βAnc-alone channels transition from a closed state, C, to an intermediate closed state, C′, before opening to O′.
evidence: This is stated in the Results section as the chosen kinetic model.

claim: The intermediate closed state in the βAnc kinetic scheme is referred to as 'flipped' or 'primed'.
source: The form of this scheme, with an intermediate closed state that precedes channel opening, is guided by models of AChR activation that include a single 'flipping' or multiple 'priming' steps (Lape et al., 2008; Mukhtasimova et al., 2016; Mukhtasimova et al., 2009). Given that for βAnc-alone channels there is a single intermediate closed state that precedes channel opening, we refer to this state in our scheme as 'flipped' or 'primed'.
evidence: This is stated in the Results section with citations to support the terminology.

claim: In the presence of acetylcholine, there was a progressive decrease in the duration of openings as the concentration of acetylcholine increased from 10 to 100 μM.
source: In the presence of acetylcholine, the single-channel current traces appeared different (Figure 4A). As the concentration of acetylcholine increased from 10 to 100 μM, there was a progressive decrease in the duration of openings, as well as a reciprocal increase in the number of short-lived closings within each burst (Figure 4A).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and shown in Figure 4A.

claim: As the concentration of acetylcholine increased from 10 to 100 μM, there was a reciprocal increase in the number of short-lived closings within each burst.
source: In the presence of acetylcholine, the single-channel current traces appeared different (Figure 4A). As the concentration of acetylcholine increased from 10 to 100 μM, there was a progressive decrease in the duration of openings, as well as a reciprocal increase in the number of short-lived closings within each burst (Figure 4A).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and shown in Figure 4A.

claim: The single-channel behaviour of βAnc-alone channels in the presence of acetylcholine is a hallmark of open-channel block.
source: This single-channel behaviour is a hallmark of open-channel block, a ubiquitous property of AChR agonists, including acetylcholine (Lape et al., 2009; Mukhtasimova et al., 2016; Ogden and Colquhoun, 1985; Sine and Steinbach, 1984).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section with citations to support the interpretation.

claim: Open-channel block is a ubiquitous property of AChR agonists, including acetylcholine.
source: This single-channel behaviour is a hallmark of open-channel block, a ubiquitous property of AChR agonists, including acetylcholine (Lape et al., 2009; Mukhtasimova et al., 2016; Ogden and Colquhoun, 1985; Sine and Steinbach, 1984).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section with citations.

claim: The same trend of open-channel block, albeit with longer-lived blocking events, was observed with QX-222.
source: Consistent with this blockage profile, the same trend, albeit with longer-lived blocking events, was observed with the well-characterized AChR open-channel blocker, 2-[(2,6-dimethylphenyl)amino]-N,N,N-trimethyl-2-oxoethaniminium chloride (QX-222) (Figure 4B; Charnet et al., 1990; Leonard et al., 1988; Pascual and Karlin, 1998).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section with citations and shown in Figure 4B.

claim: For βAnc-alone and wild-type channels, the rates of acetylcholine and QX-222 block were comparable.
source: For βAnc-alone and wild-type channels, the rates of acetylcholine and QX-222 block were comparable (see Table 1 and Table 2).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section with reference to tables containing the kinetic data.

claim: The forward rate of QX-222 block (k+B) was almost the same for both βAnc-alone and wild-type channels.
source: Of note, while the forward rate of QX-222 block (k+B) was almost the same for both types of channels, the reverse rate of QX-222 unblocking (k–B) was nearly twofold faster for βAnc-alone channels, indicating that the open pore of βAnc-alone channels has a slightly reduced affinity for QX-222.
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and supported by the kinetic data in the tables.

claim: The reverse rate of QX-222 unblocking (k–B) was nearly twofold faster for βAnc-alone channels.
source: Of note, while the forward rate of QX-222 block (k+B) was almost the same for both types of channels, the reverse rate of QX-222 unblocking (k–B) was nearly twofold faster for βAnc-alone channels, indicating that the open pore of βAnc-alone channels has a slightly reduced affinity for QX-222.
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and supported by the kinetic data in the tables.

claim: The open pore of βAnc-alone channels has a slightly reduced affinity for QX-222 compared to wild-type AChR.
source: Of note, while the forward rate of QX-222 block (k+B) was almost the same for both types of channels, the reverse rate of QX-222 unblocking (k–B) was nearly twofold faster for βAnc-alone channels, indicating that the open pore of βAnc-alone channels has a slightly reduced affinity for QX-222.
evidence: This is stated in the Results section as an inference from the kinetic data.

claim: The similarity in the profiles of acetylcholine and QX-222 block suggests that the structure of the open pore in βAnc-alone and wild-type channels is similar.
source: Regardless of this nuance, the similarity in the profiles of acetylcholine and QX-222 block suggests that the structure of the open pore in the two types of channels is similar.
evidence: This is stated in the Results section as an inference from the kinetic data.

claim: βAnc contains 125 individual substitutions and 7 deletions relative to the human β-subunit.
source: Relative to the human β-subunit, which does not form spontaneously opening homopentamers, βAnc contains 125 individual substitutions and 7 deletions (Prinston et al., 2017).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section with a citation.

claim: Not all of the 132 amino acid differences between βAnc and the human β-subunit are required for βAnc to form spontaneously opening homopentamers.
source: These 132 amino acid differences are scattered throughout the entire β-subunit, and presumably not all of them are required for βAnc to form spontaneously opening homopentamers.
evidence: This is stated in the Results section as a logical inference.

claim: The differences in amino acid sequence between βAnc and the human β-subunit are sufficient to convert the human β-subunit into a subunit capable of forming homopentamers and spontaneously opening.
source: Thus, although the differences in amino acid sequence between βAnc and the human β-subunit are sufficient to convert the human β-subunit into a subunit capable of (1) forming homopentamers and (2) spontaneously opening, the large number of residues involved, as well as their delocalised nature, obscures the subset of residues strictly necessary for either (or both) functions.
evidence: This is stated in the Results section as a conclusion from the experimental observations.

claim: βAnc homopentamers exhibit increased single-channel amplitude and conductance compared to human wild-type and βAnc-containing AChRs.
source: Compared to the human wild-type and βAnc-containing AChRs, βAnc homopentamers exhibit increased single-channel amplitude and thus conductance (Figure 2D; Figure 5; Figure 2—figure supplement 1).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and shown in the referenced figures.

claim: The increased conductance of βAnc homopentamers can be explained by amino acid differences in the second transmembrane segment (M2) of each subunit.
source: This increased conductance can be explained by amino acid differences in the second transmembrane segment (i.e. M2) of each subunit, which is one of the more conserved regions across all pLGICs.
evidence: This is stated in the Results section as an inference from structural knowledge.

claim: M2 lines the channel pore at its narrowest constriction and is a well-known determinant of single-channel conductance.
source: M2 lines the channel pore at its narrowest constriction and is a well-known determinant of single-channel conductance (Imoto et al., 1986).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section with a citation.

claim: βAnc contains acidic residues at the –4′ (Asp), –1′ (Glu), and 20′ (Asp) positions in M2.
source: This is significant because βAnc contains acidic residues at the –4′ (Asp), –1′ (Glu), and 20′ (Asp) positions, meaning that all 15 residues forming these three decisive rings are acidic, effectively maximising their negative potential (Appendix 1—figure 2).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section with reference to Appendix 1—figure 2.

claim: In βAnc homopentamers, all 15 residues forming the –4′, –1′, and 20′ rings are acidic, effectively maximising their negative potential.
source: This is significant because βAnc contains acidic residues at the –4′ (Asp), –1′ (Glu), and 20′ (Asp) positions, meaning that all 15 residues forming these three decisive rings are acidic, effectively maximising their negative potential (Appendix 1—figure 2).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section as an inference from the sequence and structure.

claim: In heteropentamers such as human wild-type and βAnc-containing AChRs, the residues contributed by individual subunits at the –4′, –1′, and 20′ positions are in some cases different, with polar/neutral (Gln) and basic (Lys) residues contributed by the ε- and δ-subunits.
source: In heteropentamers, such as human wild-type and βAnc-containing AChRs, the residues contributed by individual subunits are in some cases different, with polar/neutral (Gln) and basic (Lys) residues contributed by the ε- and δ-subunits, respectively (Appendix 1—figure 2).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section with reference to Appendix 1—figure 2.

claim: Substitution of neutral or basic residues into the –4′, –1′, or 20′ rings has been shown to reduce conductance.
source: Substitution of neutral or basic residues into any of these three rings has been shown to reduce conductance (Imoto et al., 1988).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section with a citation.

claim: The negative potential of the –4′, –1′, and 20′ rings is not maximised in human wild-type and βAnc-containing heteropentamers.
source: Thus, unlike for βAnc homopentamers that have higher conductance, the negative potential of these rings is not maximised in human wild-type and βAnc-containing heteropentamers.
evidence: This is stated in the Results section as an inference from the sequence differences.

claim: Based upon the rates of open-channel block by acetylcholine and QX-222, the structure of the open pore in βAnc homopentamers and the wild-type AChR appear to be similar.
source: Based upon the rates of open-channel block by acetylcholine and the well-known open-channel blocker, QX-222, the structure of the open pore in βAnc homopentamers and the wild-type AChR appear to be similar.
evidence: This is stated in the Results section as a conclusion from the kinetic data.

claim: βAnc homopentamers exhibit an almost twofold reduced affinity for QX-222 compared to wild-type AChR.
source: Nevertheless, kinetic fitting revealed that compared to wild-type, βAnc homopentamers exhibit an almost twofold reduced affinity for QX-222.
evidence: This is stated in the Results section based on the kinetic analysis.

claim: The 6′ and 10′ sites in M2 are known determinants of QX-222 block.
source: Specifically, the 6′ and 10′ sites are known determinants of QX-222 block (Charnet et al., 1990; Leonard et al., 1988; Pascual and Karlin, 1998), with a more polar environment at 6′, and a less polar environment at 10′, favouring interaction with QX-222 (Charnet et al., 1990).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section with citations.

claim: A more polar environment at 6′ and a less polar environment at 10′ favour interaction with QX-222.
source: Specifically, the 6′ and 10′ sites are known determinants of QX-222 block (Charnet et al., 1990; Leonard et al., 1988; Pascual and Karlin, 1998), with a more polar environment at 6′, and a less polar environment at 10′, favouring interaction with QX-222 (Charnet et al., 1990).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section with a citation.

claim: In the wild-type AChR, the polarity of the 6′ ring is limited by a hydrophobic phenylalanine residue contributed by the human β-subunit.
source: In the wild-type AChR, the polarity of the 6′ ring is limited by a hydrophobic phenylalanine residue contributed by the human β-subunit (Appendix 1—figure 2).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section with reference to Appendix 1—figure 2.

claim: In βAnc homopentamers, the 6′ ring is composed of five polar serine residues.
source: In βAnc homopentamers, the 6′ ring does not contain this phenylalanine residue and is instead composed of five polar serine residues, predicting an increased affinity for QX-222.
evidence: This is stated in the Results section based on sequence analysis.

claim: The 6′ ring composition in βAnc homopentamers predicts an increased affinity for QX-222.
source: In βAnc homopentamers, the 6′ ring does not contain this phenylalanine residue and is instead composed of five polar serine residues, predicting an increased affinity for QX-222.
evidence: This is stated in the Results section as an inference from the sequence and structural knowledge.

claim: The 10′ ring in βAnc homopentamers contains five threonine residues making it more polar than in the wild-type AChR.
source: Conversely, the 10′ ring in βAnc homopentamers contains five threonine residues making it more polar, and thus a less favourable environment for QX-222, than in the wild-type AChR, which contains two nonpolar alanine residues (from the δ- and ε-subunits) (Appendix 1—figure 2).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section with reference to Appendix 1—figure 2.

claim: The 10′ ring in βAnc homopentamers is a less favourable environment for QX-222 than in the wild-type AChR.
source: Conversely, the 10′ ring in βAnc homopentamers contains five threonine residues making it more polar, and thus a less favourable environment for QX-222, than in the wild-type AChR, which contains two nonpolar alanine residues (from the δ- and ε-subunits) (Appendix 1—figure 2).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section as an inference from the sequence and structural knowledge.

claim: The energetic contributions of the 6′ and 10′ rings to QX-222 blockage balance out such that βAnc homopentamers exhibit only a slightly reduced apparent affinity for QX-222 compared to the wild-type AChR.
source: Evidently, the energetic contributions of these two rings to QX-222 blockage balance out such that βAnc homopentamers exhibit only a slightly reduced apparent affinity for QX-222 compared to the wild-type AChR.
evidence: This is stated in the Results section as an inference from the structural analysis and kinetic data.

claim: Phylogenetic analyses of pLGICs suggest that present-day heteropentameric subunits evolved from ancestral subunits capable of self-associating to form homopentamers.
source: Phylogenetic analyses of pLGICs suggests that present-day heteropentameric subunits, such as those entrenched in the muscle-type AChR, evolved from ancestral subunits capable of self-associating to form homopentamers (Dent, 2010; Jaiteh et al., 2016; Le Novère and Changeux, 1995; Ortells, 2016; Ortells and Lunt, 1995; Pedersen et al., 2019; Tsunoyama and Gojobori, 1998).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section with multiple citations.

claim: Strictly entrenched subunits have lost compatibility between their (+) and (–) interfaces, and thus the ability to self-associate.
source: Within this framework, strictly entrenched subunits have lost compatibility between their (+) and (–) interfaces, and thus the ability to self-associate.
evidence: This is stated in the Results section as an inference from evolutionary principles.

claim: For the simplest heteropentamers made up of two types of subunits, at least one of the subunit types will have to occupy a minimum of three positions within the pentamer.
source: This is significant because the pentameric architecture of pLGICs places a constraint upon when the ability to self-associate became dispensable, and thus when strict subunit entrenchment could have evolved. For the simplest heteropentamers, made up of two types of subunits, at least one of the subunit types will have to occupy a minimum of three positions within the pentamer.
evidence: This is stated in the Results section as a logical inference from pentameric architecture.

claim: In neuronal α4β2 heteropentameric AChRs, both the α4- and β2-subunits have retained the ability to self-associate and form α4–α4 or β2–β2 interfaces.
source: Indeed, in neuronal α4β2 heteropentameric AChRs, both the α4- and β2-subunits have retained the ability to self-associate and form α4–α4 or β2–β2 interfaces, meaning that in principle, a variety of subunit stoichiometries and arrangements are possible.
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and represents established knowledge about α4β2 AChRs.

claim: The ability to self-associate is necessary but not sufficient to permit all possible heteropentameric stoichiometries and arrangements.
source: Thus, while the ability to self-associate is not sufficient to permit all possible heteropentameric stoichiometries and arrangements, it is necessary.
evidence: This is stated in the Results section as a logical inference.

claim: The subunits in the muscle-type AChR are strictly entrenched.
source: Unlike neuronal heteropentameric channels, such as α4β2 above, whose subunit stoichiometries and arrangements exhibit a degree of plasticity, the subunits in the muscle-type AChR are strictly entrenched.
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and represents established knowledge about muscle-type AChR.

claim: Strict entrenchment should only be expected in heteropentamers composed of three or more subunit types, where each of the subunits has also lost the ability to self-associate.
source: The above structural considerations imply that such strict entrenchment should only be expected in heteropentamers composed of three or more subunit types, and where each of the subunits has also lost the ability to self-associate.
evidence: This is stated in the Results section as a logical inference from structural principles.

claim: Muscle-type AChRs are made up of four types of subunits that are each incapable of self-associating and forming homopentamers.
source: Muscle-type AChRs fulfill both criteria, in that they are made up of four types of subunits that are each incapable of self-associating and forming homopentamers.
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and represents established knowledge about muscle-type AChR.

claim: Reconstructed ancestral β-subunits retain the ability to self-associate and form homomers, suggesting that the ancestral β-subunits were not strictly entrenched.
source: The finding that reconstructed ancestral β-subunits retain the ability to self-associate and form homomers, suggests that, unlike their extant human and Torpedo counterparts, the ancestral β-subunits were not strictly entrenched, and that their entrenchment occurred in parallel lineages after the last common ancestor shared by humans and Torpediniformes (i.e. Gnathostomata).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section as an inference from the experimental findings.

claim: The entrenchment of β-subunits occurred in parallel lineages after the last common ancestor shared by humans and Torpediniformes (i.e. Gnathostomata).
source: The finding that reconstructed ancestral β-subunits retain the ability to self-associate and form homomers, suggests that, unlike their extant human and Torpedo counterparts, the ancestral β-subunits were not strictly entrenched, and that their entrenchment occurred in parallel lineages after the last common ancestor shared by humans and Torpediniformes (i.e. Gnathostomata).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section as an inference from the experimental findings and phylogenetic context.

claim: βAncS has 67 substitutions and 6 indels relative to βAnc.
source: We have shown that an alternate ancestral β-subunit (βAncS), with 67 substitutions and 6 indels relative to βAnc, was still able to form homomers that opened spontaneously.
evidence: This is stated in the Results section based on sequence comparison.

claim: βAncS was still able to form homomers that opened spontaneously.
source: We have shown that an alternate ancestral β-subunit (βAncS), with 67 substitutions and 6 indels relative to βAnc, was still able to form homomers that opened spontaneously.
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and demonstrated by experimental data.

claim: Spontaneous openings of βAncS homomers occurred in bursts that contained brief closings (i.e. 'nachschlag shuttings') and had an open probability that exceeded 0.90.
source: Furthermore, spontaneous openings of βAncS homomers also occurred in bursts that contained brief closings (i.e. 'nachschlag shuttings') and had an open probability that exceeded 0.90.
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and demonstrated by experimental data.

claim: The ability of βAnc to form spontaneously opening homomers is robust to substantial variations in the inferred ancestral β-subunit amino acid sequence.
source: These findings demonstrate that the ability of βAnc to form spontaneously opening homomers is robust to substantial variations in the inferred ancestral β-subunit amino acid sequence.
evidence: This is stated in the Results section as a conclusion from the βAncS experiments.

claim: The capacity of reconstructed ancestral β-subunits to form spontaneously opening homomers is deeply embedded in their structure and evolutionary history.
source: Thus, the capacity of these reconstructed ancestral β-subunits to form spontaneously opening homomers is deeply embedded in their structure and evolutionary history.
evidence: This is stated in the Results section as a conclusion from the robustness to sequence variation.

claim: The kinetic behaviour of βAncS homomers was more complex than originally observed with βAnc.
source: The kinetic behaviour of βAncS homomers was more complex than originally observed with βAnc.
evidence: This is stated in the Results section based on kinetic analysis.

claim: The increased complexity of βAncS kinetics necessitated the expansion of the original scheme used to fit βAnc to include two additional priming steps.
source: This increased complexity necessitated the expansion of the original scheme used to fit βAnc to include two additional priming steps.
evidence: This is stated in the Results section based on kinetic modeling.

claim: Both the original βAnc and expanded βAncS schemes parallel the scheme used to describe the muscle-type AChR, which included two priming steps.
source: Both the original βAnc and expanded βAncS schemes parallel the scheme used to describe the muscle-type AChR, which included two priming steps (i.e. 'singly' and 'doubly' primed) that each correlated with conformational changes around the two agonist-binding sites (Mukhtasimova et al., 2009).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section with a citation.

claim: In the muscle-type AChR scheme, the two priming steps correlated with conformational changes around the two agonist-binding sites.
source: Both the original βAnc and expanded βAncS schemes parallel the scheme used to describe the muscle-type AChR, which included two priming steps (i.e. 'singly' and 'doubly' primed) that each correlated with conformational changes around the two agonist-binding sites (Mukhtasimova et al., 2009).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section with a citation.

claim: For βAncS, which lacks agonist-binding sites, the different levels of priming correlate with conformational changes occurring within individual subunits.
source: In the case of βAncS, which lacks agonist-binding sites, the simplest interpretation is that the different levels of priming correlate with conformational changes occurring within individual subunits.
evidence: This is stated in the Results section as an inference from the kinetic model.

claim: Priming is an important step in the activation of both βAncS and βAnc homopentamers.
source: Regardless of the interpretation, priming is an important step in the activation of both βAncS and βAnc homopentamers.
evidence: This is stated in the Results section as a conclusion from the kinetic analysis.

claim: Modern mechanisms of AChR activation include intermediate closed states, which place the roots of agonism at a stage in the activation process that precedes channel opening.
source: Modern mechanisms of AChR activation include intermediate closed states, which place the roots of agonism at a stage in the activation process that precedes channel opening (Lape et al., 2008; Mukhtasimova et al., 2016; Mukhtasimova et al., 2009).
evidence: This is stated in the Discussion with citations.

claim: A consequence of modern AChR activation mechanisms is that the ultimate opening and closing rates of the channel are independent of agonist.
source: A consequence of these mechanisms is that the ultimate opening and closing rates of the channel are independent of agonist.
evidence: This is stated in the Discussion as an inference from the cited mechanisms.

claim: Additional single-channel hallmarks of AChR function are independent of agonist, as they occur in spontaneously opening homopentameric channels that are devoid of agonist-binding sites.
source: Here, we have shown that additional single-channel hallmarks of AChR function are independent of agonist, as they occur in spontaneously opening homopentameric channels that are devoid of agonist-binding sites, and which are formed from reconstructed ancestral AChR β-subunits.
evidence: This is stated in the Discussion as a conclusion from the experimental findings.

claim: The β-subunit is the least conserved of the four AChR subunits.
source: Often overlooked, the β-subunit is the least conserved of the four AChR subunits, and is the only subunit that does not contribute residues to the two AChR agonist-binding sites.
evidence: This is stated in the Discussion and represents established knowledge about AChR subunits.

claim: Hallmarks of AChR function remain deeply embedded in β-subunit sequence, structure, and evolutionary history.
source: Despite these considerations, hallmarks of AChR function remain deeply embedded in β-subunit sequence, structure, and evolutionary history.
evidence: This is stated in the Discussion as a conclusion from the experimental findings.

claim: The functional hallmarks of AChR that are independent of agonist may predate agonism.
source: Given that these functional hallmarks are independent of agonist, it is tempting to speculate that they predate agonism, and thus that agonism evolved subsequently as an additional layer of regulation in this family of pentameric ion channels.
evidence: This is stated in the Discussion as speculation based on the findings.

claim: Agonism may have evolved subsequently as an additional layer of regulation in the pLGIC family.
source: Given that these functional hallmarks are independent of agonist, it is tempting to speculate that they predate agonism, and thus that agonism evolved subsequently as an additional layer of regulation in this family of pentameric ion channels.
evidence: This is stated in the Discussion as speculation based on the findings.

claim: When transfected alone, βAnc forms functional ion channels that exhibit a single, uniform amplitude distributed around a mean of ~16 pA.
source: When βAnc is expressed alone, the resulting channels exhibit a single, uniform amplitude, distributed around a mean of ~16 pA (Figure 5A and D), making the wild-type βAnc subunit an ideal HC subunit for electrical fingerprinting.
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and shown in Figure 5A and D.

claim: βAnc harbouring three arginine residues (E420R, D424R, and E428R) exhibited a reduced single-channel amplitude centred around ~1–2 pA.
source: When βAnc harbouring three arginines in this region was transfected by itself, the resulting channels exhibited a reduced single-channel amplitude centred around~1–2pA (Figure 5B and D).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and shown in Figure 5B and D.

claim: When cDNAs encoding HC and LC variants of βAnc were transfected together, a variety of single-channel amplitudes were observed in each patch.
source: When cDNAs encoding HC and LC variants of βAnc were transfected together, a variety of single-channel amplitudes were observed in each patch (Figure 5C).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and shown in Figure 5C.

claim: The amplitudes from HC and LC βAnc cotransfection segregated into as many as six amplitude classes.
source: Constructing event-based amplitude histograms, and pooling amplitudes from more than one recording, revealed that the amplitudes segregated into as many as six amplitude classes, with the highest and lowest amplitude classes matching that of the HC and LC forms of βAnc-alone channels.
evidence: This is stated in the Results section based on amplitude histogram analysis.

claim: The difference in amplitude between successive classes was somewhat regular, demonstrating five approximately equal contributions to single-channel conductance.
source: The difference in amplitude between successive classes was somewhat regular, demonstrating five approximately equal contributions to single-channel conductance (Figure 5D), consistent with the hypothesis that βAnc-alone channels are homopentamers.
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and shown in Figure 5D.

claim: The electrical fingerprinting results are consistent with the hypothesis that βAnc-alone channels are homopentamers.
source: The difference in amplitude between successive classes was somewhat regular, demonstrating five approximately equal contributions to single-channel conductance (Figure 5D), consistent with the hypothesis that βAnc-alone channels are homopentamers.
evidence: This is stated in the Results section as a conclusion from the electrical fingerprinting experiment.

claim: Reconstruction of βAnc was based upon a molecular phylogeny that diverged from the accepted species phylogeny.
source: As noted previously, reconstruction of βAnc was based upon a molecular phylogeny that diverged from the accepted species phylogeny (Emlaw et al., 2021; Emlaw et al., 2020; Prinston et al., 2017; Tessier et al., 2017).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section with citations.

claim: βAncS reconstruction was based upon a molecular phylogeny that matched the accepted species phylogeny.
source: To test this, we took advantage of an alternate ancestral β-subunit, called 'βAncS', whose reconstruction was based upon a molecular phylogeny that matched the accepted species phylogeny (Emlaw et al., 2021).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section with a citation.

claim: The ability of βAnc to form homomers that spontaneously open is not an artefact of the phylogeny used to reconstruct it.
source: This demonstrated that the ability of βAnc to form homomers that spontaneously open is not an artefact of the phylogeny used to reconstruct it.
evidence: This is stated in the Results section as a conclusion from the βAncS experiments.

claim: The ability of βAnc to form spontaneously opening homomers is robust to the phylogenetic uncertainties inherent in ancestral sequence reconstruction.
source: Instead, this surprising ability of βAnc is robust to the phylogenetic uncertainties inherent in ancestral sequence reconstruction, as well as substantial variation in the amino acid sequence of the reconstructed ancestral β-subunits.
evidence: This is stated in the Results section as a conclusion from the βAncS experiments.

claim: Single-channel bursts of βAncS were heterogeneous, displaying at least three distinct kinetic behaviours.
source: While βAncS forms homomers that open spontaneously, inspection of the βAncS single-channel activity revealed additional complexity not seen with βAnc. For βAncS, single-channel bursts were heterogeneous, displaying at least three distinct kinetic behaviours (Figure 6B).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and shown in Figure 6B.

claim: In some cases, the kinetic behaviour of βAncS changed within a burst, demonstrating that the different kinetics were possible within the same channel.
source: In some cases, the kinetic behaviour changed within a burst, demonstrating that the different kinetics were possible within the same channel (Figure 6B; boxed).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and shown in Figure 6B.

claim: The heterogeneity in βAncS kinetics was reflected in apparent open and closed duration histograms, with each displaying a minimum of three exponential components.
source: This heterogeneity was also reflected in apparent open and closed duration histograms, with each displaying a minimum of three exponential components (Figure 6C).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and shown in Figure 6C.

claim: The increased number of exponential components in βAncS indicated additional open and closed states relative to βAnc.
source: The increased number of exponential components indicated additional open and closed states relative to βAnc, and thus that the three-state scheme used to fit βAnc was insufficient to describe the spontaneous activity of βAncS.
evidence: This is stated in the Results section as an inference from the kinetic analysis.

claim: The three-state scheme used to fit βAnc was insufficient to describe the spontaneous activity of βAncS.
source: The increased number of exponential components indicated additional open and closed states relative to βAnc, and thus that the three-state scheme used to fit βAnc was insufficient to describe the spontaneous activity of βAncS.
evidence: This is stated in the Results section as a conclusion from the kinetic analysis.

claim: The expanded scheme for βAncS includes two additional 'priming' steps, where openings could occur from one of three primed states.
source: To account for the additional states, we expanded our original scheme to include two additional 'priming' steps, where openings could occur from one of three primed states (Figure 6D).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and shown in Figure 6D.

claim: The expanded βAncS scheme builds directly upon the one used to fit muscle-type AChRs that had been engineered to open spontaneously.
source: This scheme, with multiple priming steps, builds directly upon the one used to fit muscle-type AChRs that had been engineered to open spontaneously (Mukhtasimova et al., 2009).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section with a citation.

claim: In accord with the muscle-type AChR, the equilibrium gating constants for βAncS appear to increase for each successive priming step.
source: Nevertheless, we note that in accord with the muscle-type AChR, the equilibrium gating constants appear to increase (Table 3; compare Θ1, Θ2, and Θ3), and thus the open states become more and more favoured, for each successive priming step.
evidence: This is stated in the Results section based on the kinetic fitting results.

claim: A scheme with multiple stages of priming is adequate to describe the complex spontaneous single-channel activity of βAncS homomers.
source: In any case, the fits suggest that a scheme of this form, with multiple stages of priming, is adequate to describe the complex spontaneous single-channel activity of βAncS homomers.
evidence: This is stated in the Results section as a conclusion from the kinetic modeling.

claim: βAnc can both incorporate into heteropentameric AChRs and self-associate to form homopentameric βAnc channels.
source: Evidently, βAnc can both incorporate into heteropentameric AChRs (Emlaw et al., 2021), and self-associate to form homopentameric βAnc channels.
evidence: This is stated in the Discussion as a conclusion from the experimental findings.

claim: Reducing the overall expression of AChR subunits was sufficient to tip the balance between the incorporation of βAnc into hetero- versus homopentamers.
source: Reducing the overall expression of AChR subunits was sufficient to tip the balance between the incorporation of βAnc into hetero- versus homopentamers, and thus unmask this previously unobserved ability of βAnc to form homomeric channels.
evidence: This is stated in the Discussion as an inference from the experimental observations.

claim: Modern-day muscle-type β-subunits do not appear to form homopentamers.
source: At first glance, the ability of βAnc to form homopentamers is unexpected. Modern-day muscle-type β-subunits do not appear to form homopentamers, and instead appear fully entrenched within heteropentameric muscle-type AChRs.
evidence: This is stated in the Discussion and represents established knowledge.

claim: Modern-day muscle-type β-subunits appear fully entrenched within heteropentameric muscle-type AChRs.
source: At first glance, the ability of βAnc to form homopentamers is unexpected. Modern-day muscle-type β-subunits do not appear to form homopentamers, and instead appear fully entrenched within heteropentameric muscle-type AChRs.
evidence: This is stated in the Discussion and represents established knowledge.

claim: The ability to revert the muscle-type β-subunit back to a subunit capable of forming homopentamers attests to the presumed homopentameric origins of pentameric ligand-gated ion channel subunits.
source: From an evolutionary perspective, this ability to revert the muscle-type β-subunit, which is entrenched in a heteropentamer, back to a subunit capable of forming homopentamers, attests to the presumed homopentameric origins of pentameric ligand-gated ion channel subunits (Ortells and Lunt, 1995).
evidence: This is stated in the Discussion with a citation as an inference from the findings.

claim: Some of the first single-channel recordings of frog AChRs activated by agonists revealed that agonist-activated openings occur in quick succession, as bursts of activity originating from the same channel.
source: Some of the first single-channel recordings of frog AChRs activated by agonists revealed that agonist-activated openings occur in quick succession, as bursts of activity originating from the same channel (Sakmann et al., 1980).
evidence: This is stated in the Discussion with a citation.

claim: The main effect of increasing the concentration of agonist was to increase the open probability within bursts.
source: The main effect of increasing the concentration of agonist was to increase the open probability within bursts, with saturating concentrations of full agonists, such as acetylcholine, leading to bursts where the open probability exceeded 0.90 (i.e. the channel was open for more than 90% of the duration of the burst).
evidence: This is stated in the Discussion and represents established knowledge about AChR activation.

claim: Saturating concentrations of full agonists, such as acetylcholine, lead to bursts where the open probability exceeded 0.90.
source: The main effect of increasing the concentration of agonist was to increase the open probability within bursts, with saturating concentrations of full agonists, such as acetylcholine, leading to bursts where the open probability exceeded 0.90 (i.e. the channel was open for more than 90% of the duration of the burst).
evidence: This is stated in the Discussion and represents established knowledge about AChR activation.

claim: Despite the absence of agonist, activation of βAnc homopentamers appears efficient, with the probability of being open within a burst exceeding 0.90.
source: Spontaneous openings of βAnc homopentamers also occur in bursts, and despite the absence of agonist, activation appears efficient, with the probability of being open within a burst also exceeding 0.90.
evidence: This is stated in the Discussion based on the experimental data.

claim: It was originally proposed that the duration of nachschlag shuttings was related to agonist efficacy.
source: This is significant because it was originally proposed that the duration of nachschlag shuttings was related to agonist efficacy (Colquhoun and Sakmann, 1981).
evidence: This is stated in the Discussion with a citation.

claim: Subsequent work showed that nachschlag shuttings were independent of agonist.
source: However, subsequent work showed that nachschlag shuttings were independent of agonist, which necessitated the introduction of an additional closed state appended to the agonist-activated open state in early schemes of AChR activation (Sine and Steinbach, 1986).
evidence: This is stated in the Discussion with a citation.

claim: The finding that nachschlag shuttings were independent of agonist necessitated the introduction of an additional closed state appended to the agonist-activated open state in early schemes of AChR activation.
source: However, subsequent work showed that nachschlag shuttings were independent of agonist, which necessitated the introduction of an additional closed state appended to the agonist-activated open state in early schemes of AChR activation (Sine and Steinbach, 1986).
evidence: This is stated in the Discussion with a citation.

claim: The finding that nachschlag shuttings were independent of agonist was some of the impetus for refined schemes, where the additional closed states preceded channel opening and were referred to as 'flipped' or 'primed'.
source: This latter finding was some of the impetus for refined schemes, where the additional closed states preceded channel opening and were referred to as 'flipped' or 'primed' (Lape et al., 2008; Mukhtasimova et al., 2009).
evidence: This is stated in the Discussion with citations.
